svg.title: The batch keeps its rows through both layers
svg.desc: Every array of the forward pass for the post's batch of 3 samples, each product drawn with its left factor beside the result and its right factor above it. Layer 1: the input X, shape (3, 4), rows one per sample, holds 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.0, 5.0, minus 1.0, 2.0, minus 1.5, 2.7, 3.3, minus 0.8; above the result sits W1 transposed, shape (4, 3), whose column k holds the weights of neuron k: 0.2, 0.5, minus 0.26, 0.8, minus 0.91, minus 0.27, minus 0.5, 0.26, 0.17, 1.0, minus 0.5, 0.87; under it the bias b1, shape (3,), 2.0, 3.0, 0.5, added to every row. The result Z1, shape (3, 3), holds 4.8, 1.21, 2.385, 8.9, minus 1.81, 0.2, 1.41, 1.051, 0.026. Z1 is also the left factor of layer 2: above the second result sit W2 transposed, shape (3, 3), 0.1, minus 0.5, minus 0.44, minus 0.14, 0.12, 0.73, 0.5, minus 0.33, minus 0.13, and the bias b2, minus 1.0, 2.0, minus 0.5. The result Z2, shape (3, 3), holds 0.5031, minus 1.04185, minus 2.03875, 0.2434, minus 2.7332, minus 5.7633, minus 0.99314, 1.41254, minus 0.35655. A note at the top left explains that row i on the left meets column k above at entry (i, k) of the result; under it the two layer calls, Z1 = X W1 transposed + b1 and Z2 = Z1 W2 transposed + b2, and the same calls in the snippet's code, np.dot(inputs, weights1.T) + biases1 and np.dot(layer1_outputs, weights2.T) + biases2. Row 1 of Z1, column 1 of W2 transposed and the first bias of b2 are outlined, and one arrow from the row and one from the bias point into the top-left entry of Z2, 0.5031, which the caption line works out: 0.1 times 4.8, minus 0.14 times 1.21, plus 0.5 times 2.385, minus 1.0.
